items.title: Section: Never Making a Petitioner Wait, and Four Kinds of Giving Entirely Free of Ulterior Motive

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，不令求者數數來求，往還親附，隨順繫屬，稽留疲倦，然後方施，唯暫來求即便施與。
items.en: Bodhisattvas never make a petitioner come again and again, growing dependent and weary, before finally giving; the moment someone comes to ask, the gift is given.

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，不依世間名聲讚頌而行布施，不依於他反報恩德而行布施，不依帝釋、魔王、輪王、自在等果而行布施，亦復不為誑誘他故而行惠施。
items.en: Bodhisattvas do not give for the sake of worldly fame or praise, nor expecting the recipient's gratitude in return, nor for the sake of a future rebirth as Śakra, as Māra, as a wheel-turning king, as Īśvara, or the like, nor for the sake of deceiving or manipulating another.

items.zh: 謂欲令他國王、大臣、城邑聚落諸婆羅門、多饒財寶長者、居士、大富商主、施者施主知我行施，定當恭敬、尊重、讚歎、供養於我，故行惠施。

items.title: A Generous Heart Regardless of Means, and Never Sowing Division Through a Gift

items.zh: 又不狹劣而行惠施。謂財雖少，尚廣心施，何況財多。又不誑他而行惠施。謂先於彼少行惠施，令起愛著、令親附己，然後傾滅。
items.en: Nor is giving ever narrow or meager: even with little wealth, one still gives with an expansive heart, how much more so with abundant wealth. Nor does one give deceptively: first offering small kindness to someone so as to draw out their attachment and dependence, only to then destroy them.

items.zh: 又復不為乖離於他而行惠施。謂我以施乖離村邑、村邑一分，乖離國土、國土一分，令背其主而來屬我。
items.en: Nor does one give in order to sow division: giving so as to draw a village, or part of one, or a territory, or part of one, away from its rightful ruler and towards oneself instead.

items.title: Leading by Example, and Distributing Fairly Among a Crowd

items.zh: 又諸菩薩翹勤無惰起策具足，勇銳自嚴。先自行施，後勸他施。非自懈怠，策他勤施。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, diligent and never lax, fully rousing themselves, courageous and self-disciplined, first practice giving themselves, and only then encourage others to give — never lax themselves while urging others to be diligent.

items.zh: 又無量眾同集來乞，如實了知持戒、犯戒，隨其長幼以次而坐，從上至下周旋往返，窮諸施物分布與之。
items.en: When countless beings gather together seeking alms, knowing truly who among them keeps or has broken precepts, one nonetheless seats them simply by seniority, moving from the front to the back and around again, exhausting every gift by distributing it among them all.

items.title: Giving Without Artificial Limit, and Never Harming Anyone in the Course of It

items.zh: 又諸菩薩現有無量廣多財物，終不行於有量之施。
items.en: Bodhisattvas who genuinely possess vast and abundant wealth never give only some artificially limited amount.

items.zh: 又諸菩薩不損惱他而行惠施。謂不訶罵、捶打、恐怖、毀辱、縛害、拘禁、斫刺、驅擯於此，而施於彼。
items.en: Bodhisattvas do not harm one being in order to give to another — not through cursing, striking, threatening, humiliating, binding, imprisoning, wounding, or expelling one being in order to give the resulting gain to someone else.

items.title: Joy Before, Purity During, No Regret After — And Never a Counterfeit Gift

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，施前意悅，施時心淨，施後無悔。
items.en: Bodhisattvas feel genuine joy before giving, hold a mind free of clinging while giving, and feel no regret whatsoever after giving.

items.zh: 又諸菩薩不以諂詭而行惠施。謂終不以非實末尼、真珠、琉璃、珂貝、璧玉、珊瑚等寶，而施希望真實寶者。
items.en: Bodhisattvas do not give deceptively: never giving a counterfeit gem, pearl, lapis, coral, or similar treasure to someone hoping for a genuine one.

items.title: Section: Giving as Simply Returning What Was Never One's Own

items.zh: 又諸菩薩所有財物若少、若多，無不運心先施一切。後來求者，如取自財，菩薩與時，如還彼物。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, regarding all their wealth, whether little or much, have already, in mind, given it entirely to everyone from the start. When someone later comes seeking it, it is as though they simply take what is already their own; and when the bodhisattva gives, it is as though returning that object to them.

items.title: Free of Every Remaining Fault — Timed Well, Properly Mannered, With an Undistracted Mind

items.zh: 又諸菩薩應時而施，不以非時；自他淨施，非不清淨；合儀而施，不以非儀；無亂心施，不以散亂。
items.en: Bodhisattvas give at a fitting time, not an unfitting one; give with a mind clean whether acting themselves or through another, never uncleanly; give in a manner that is proper, never improper; and give with an undistracted mind, never a scattered one.

items.title: Section: Never Mocking a Petitioner, Giving Freely to Whoever Helps Themselves — Thirty-One Points Conclude

items.zh: 又諸菩薩見來求者，終不嗤笑，亦不輕弄，亦不令其而生𧹞愧；亦不顰蹙，舒顏平視，前笑先言；終不稽留，疾疾而施。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, seeing someone come to ask, never mock them, never belittle them, never cause them shame; nor do they frown, but greet them with an open expression and a warm word first; and never make them wait, giving swiftly.

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，他雖不求，自恣求者必有所求，稱須而與，常開求者歡情自取。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, even when no one has specifically asked, let anyone who comes seek freely whatever they genuinely need, providing exactly what is needed, keeping it always openly available for whoever wishes to take it for themselves.

items.title: Section: Giving With Genuine Skilful Wisdom Opens

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，不以惡慧而行布施，常以巧慧而行布施。云何菩薩巧慧布施？
items.en: Bodhisattvas do not give guided by misguided, unwholesome wisdom, but constantly give guided by genuine skilful wisdom. What is a bodhisattva's giving guided by skilful wisdom?

items.title: Section: Skilful Giving With Wealth — Prioritising the Desperate, Gently Declining the Comfortable

items.zh: 謂諸菩薩現有種種可施財物，求者未至，先發是心：設二求者俱來我所，一是安樂、非貧非賤、有依有怙；二是危苦、是貧是賤、無依無怙。我於爾時，應自揆量所有財物，若堪於二充足滿願，即應俱施滿願充足。如其財物不堪於二充足滿願，即應方便發遣安樂、非貧非賤、有依有怙，盡己所有施彼危苦、是貧是賤、無依無怙。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, possessing various objects that could be given, resolve in advance, before any petitioner arrives: should two petitioners come to me at once, one comfortable, neither poor nor lowly, with support and protection, and the other in genuine crisis, poor and lowly, without any support or protection, I should weigh my own wealth. If it can fully satisfy both, I give fully to satisfy both. If it cannot satisfy both, I should skilfully send away the one who is comfortable, neither poor nor lowly, with support and protection, and give everything I have to the one in genuine crisis, poor and lowly, without support or protection.

items.zh: 發是心已，如所思惟，即便成辦如是事業。
於安樂等諸來求者，既無力能足滿其願，先當方便發意思惟，辭謝發遣：我此施物，於危苦等先捨先許，故今與之；非我於汝無樂施心，但更無力。唯願賢首，勿於我所嫌恨棄背。
items.en: Towards a comfortable petitioner one lacks the means to fully satisfy, one first considers carefully how to graciously decline: this gift was already promised in advance to someone in genuine crisis, which is why it goes to them now; it is not that I have no wish to give to you, only that I have no further means. I only hope, good friend, that you will not hold this against me or turn away in resentment.

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，現有種種可施財物，知有慳家、最極慳家、悋執財寶，慳固兢戰，於其家中，曾未惠施一切沙門、婆羅門等。

blocks.text: Thirty-one points of right giving conclude, and the treatise turns to giving "guided by skilful wisdom".

"Bodhisattvas never make a petitioner come again and again; the moment someone asks, it is given." "Not for fame or praise, nor expecting gratitude, nor for a future rebirth as Śakra, Māra, or a universal monarch."

"Even with little wealth, one gives with an expansive heart." Never "first offering small kindness to win trust, then taking more" (Master Cháng Bǎi: a ruthless method, but common), nor giving to draw people away from their rightful ruler.
One gives first, then encourages others. In a crowd, "one seats them by seniority, from front to back", so none leaves disappointed.
Those with abundant wealth do not give "an artificially limited amount". "One does not harm one being to give to another."
"Joy before giving, a mind free of clinging while giving, no regret after." Never a counterfeit gem.

subs.head: Returning what was never one's own

blocks.text: "Bodhisattvas, regarding all their wealth, have already in mind given it to everyone. When someone later asks, it is as though they simply take back what is theirs." Venerable Miào Jìng: "I owe you this, and now return it."
"They never mock or shame a petitioner, nor frown, but greet them with an open expression and a warm word first."

If two petitioners come at once, one comfortable and one in crisis, and one cannot satisfy both, "I should skilfully send away the comfortable one, and give everything to the one in need": gently: "It is not that I have no wish to give to you, only that I have no further means."

quiz.q: According to the treatise, when does the bodhisattva give to someone who asks?
options: after they have come many times and grown weary
the moment someone comes to ask
quiz.why: "Bodhisattvas never make a petitioner come again and again, growing dependent and weary, before finally giving; the moment someone comes to ask, the gift is given." Venerable Miào Jìng: refusing the first time and giving only after many visits — bodhisattvas do not do that.

quiz.q: The English renders this as "a future rebirth as a great ruler among gods or humans." Compared with Master Cháng Bǎi, what is lost?
options: the original lists four rewards — Śakra, the Māra king, a wheel-turning king, Maheśvara; the English merges them, and Māra disappears
the original mentions only human kings
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: not giving for the sake of being reborn as Śakra, the Māra king, a wheel-turning king, or Maheśvara — and these, with fame and gratitude, make up the cases of giving without ulterior dependence. The English compresses the four into "a great ruler."

quiz.q: "Nor does one give deceptively." How do the lectures describe such deceptive giving?
options: giving to those who don't need it
first offering small favours to get close, with a hidden scheme, then ruining the person and taking their wealth
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: this method is ruthless, yet worldly people often do it — first small favours to get close, with a hidden scheme behind them. Venerable Miào Jìng: then they ruin you and take all your wealth.

quiz.q: When countless beings gather to ask, they are seated "by seniority." How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain "seniority"?
options: the order of their years since ordination
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: they are seated in order of their years since ordination, so that no one leaves disappointed without receiving anything.

quiz.q: How does the treatise describe the bodhisattva's mind before, during, and after giving?
options: joyful before, pure while giving, no regret after
quiz.why: "Bodhisattvas feel genuine joy before giving, hold a mind free of clinging while giving, and feel no regret whatsoever after giving." Master Cháng Bǎi: while giving, the mind is pure — self, other, and gift are not taken as real; the three spheres are empty.

quiz.q: "When someone later comes seeking it, it is as though they take what is their own; when the bodhisattva gives, it is as though returning it." How do the lectures describe the bodhisattva's attitude?
options: as if one owed it to them and is now repaying; beings need it, and one is simply giving it back
like a loan to be recovered
like alms tossed down to a beggar
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: it is as if "I owe you this and am now giving it back" — that is the attitude. Master Cháng Bǎi: beings need it, and one is simply returning it to them.

quiz.q: When declining the comfortable petitioner, the bodhisattva says, "I only hope, good friend, that you will not hold this against me." How does Master Cháng Bǎi describe the right manner of declining?
options: very courteous — don't just say there's none, don't be so blunt; give reasons so they are convinced
quiz.why: "It is not that I have no wish to give to you, only that I have no further means. I only hope, good friend, that you will not hold this against me." Master Cháng Bǎi: be very courteous — don't just say there's nothing left, don't be so curt; explain the reason so the other person is convinced.
